proposed_widenings.name: suppress_concentration_break
proposed_widenings.justification: No atom expresses 'taking damage cannot break concentration on [specific spell]'. The mechanic is full immunity to the damage-induced concentration check, scoped to a named spell. This is distinct from advantage (modify_roll_advantage) and from any existing saveSourceFilter variant. The v4 taxonomy has no concept for this.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Taking damage can't break your Concentration on Hunter's Mark.

proposed_widenings.name: saveSourceFilter { kind: 'damage_induced_concentration_check'; spellId: string }
proposed_widenings.justification: Even if a suppress/immunity mode were added to modify_roll_advantage, scoping it to 'concentration checks specifically caused by taking damage for a named spell' requires a new saveSourceFilter variant. The existing variant only covers 'spell_or_other_magical_effect' and cannot express the concentration-break-on-damage trigger scoped to a specific spell.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Taking damage can't break your Concentration on Hunter's Mark.

notes: The feature is a passive always-on grant (family=passive is fine) but needs a new atom to express its payload. The closest existing atom is modify_roll_advantage with saveSourceFilter, but: (1) the mode would need a new 'auto_success'/'immune' variant rather than advantage/disadvantage, and (2) there is no filter shape for 'damage-induced concentration check for spell X'. A dedicated atom suppress_concentration_break { spellId: string } is the cleanest design — it maps to a single v4-style effect atom and the passive family encodes everything else correctly.
